title: Molecular Rewiring and Compensatory Mechanisms Sustain DNA Recognition in the Mutant ZTA Transcription Factor: Insights from Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
one_liner_zh: 该文通过全原子分子动力学模拟和MM/PBSA方法，系统研究了突变ZTA转录因子与DNA复合物中相互作用网络的重组与补偿机制，核心聚焦TF-DNA结合识别与动态机理，方法为物理模拟，高度匹配本课题。
abstract: Protein-DNA complexes are stabilized by various interactions through an interaction network between protein and DNA. Any change in the system horizontal line whether through mutations in protein/DNA, external factors, or protein conformational transitions horizontal line can alter the interaction network, affecting structural and functional aspects. Employing all-atom classical molecular dynamics, we investigated how the interaction network in ZTA-DNA is rewired, while key arginine residues in ZTA are mutated to oppositely charged glutamic acids. Using the MM/PBSA technique, we computed per-residue binding energies and correlated them with structural features. A detailed mechanistic study shows that mutations in key arginine residues form new interactions either around the mutation site and/or in the other ZTA monomer. Through load-sharing system attempts to counterbalance the interaction load, leading to reorganization of the existing interaction network. From single- to double-site mutations, the complex partially maintains its structural stability through additional interactions formed by lysine, particularly K178, while multisite mutations cannot sustain its structural stability, leading to system destabilization. Despite inherent structural symmetry in ZTA, an asymmetric monomer contribution is observed upon mutation. The binding affinity of the ZTA-DNA complex shows a good correlation with structural and interaction features, following the trend A > E  approximately  D > C >> B. Overall, our rigorous mechanistic study provides deeper insights into the interaction network reorganization mechanism in the ZTA-DNA system. Since ZTA is a key factor in the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), this study will be central to understanding DNA recognition and developing drug therapeutics targeting viral transcription factors in EBV.
abstract_zh: 蛋白-DNA复合物通过蛋白质与DNA之间的相互作用网络，由多种相互作用稳定。系统中任何变化——无论是蛋白质/DNA的突变、外部因素，还是蛋白质构象转变——都可能改变相互作用网络，影响结构和功能方面。采用全原子经典分子动力学，我们研究了当ZTA中的关键精氨酸残基被突变为带相反电荷的谷氨酸时，ZTA-DNA中的相互作用网络如何被重新布线。利用MM/PBSA技术，我们计算了每个残基的结合能，并将其与结构特征相关联。一项详细的机制研究表明，关键精氨酸残基的突变会在突变位点附近和/或另一个ZTA单体中形成新的相互作用。通过负载分担系统试图平衡相互作用负载，导致现有相互作用网络的重组。从单位点突变到双位点突变，复合物通过赖氨酸（特别是K178）形成的额外相互作用部分维持其结构稳定性，而多位点突变则无法维持其结构稳定性，导致系统失稳。尽管ZTA具有固有的结构对称性，但在突变时观察到不对称的单体贡献。ZTA-DNA复合物的结合亲和力与结构和相互作用特征显示出良好的相关性，遵循趋势A > E ≈ D > C >> B。总体而言，我们严谨的机制研究为ZTA-DNA系统中相互作用网络重组机制提供了更深入的见解。由于ZTA是爱泼斯坦-巴尔病毒（EBV）中的关键因子，这项研究将对理解DNA识别以及开发靶向EBV病毒转录因子的药物疗法至关重要。
